timing: Canonical ClientResult.started_at/completed_at, cross-checked against immutable entrypoint log ordering and native benchmark rates for all eight built-in cases. Independent-client throughput uses earliest start to latest completion, including start skew and drain.
cost: Actual Slurm GPU count times each actual array-task elapsed seconds / 3600, including all attempts, startup and shutdown. Both independent task IDs are charged once; parent summaries are not double counted. GPU-hours are not full monetary cost. The eight-record smoke gate is excluded from comparative trial totals.
validation: Draft 2020-12 schema validity, JSON parsing and conformance; schema wrapper unwrapped when present.
limitations: One trial per point, no confidence intervals. Experimental build includes timing PR1173 and proxy PR1174; not a released version. Connector limit0 removes its active-connection cap; the separate backend waiting-request guard remains128. Physical KV/token budgets and adaptive client backoff also affect execution. Highest tested ceiling is not a hardware maximum. Independent comparison changes client/proxy count, client CPU and shard size. No production-scale generation or interrupted-generation recovery test.
projection_note: Untested one-million-valid projections: rate times (14400 - measured pre-client seconds - ceil(measured post-client seconds)); whole allocations rounded up. Full-budget GPU-hours reserve four hours per allocation. Excludes queue wait, safety margin, failures and scaling variability. Four fixed allocation slots compare32 versus64 simultaneous GPUs; a fixed32-GPU budget permits four one-node or two two-node allocations.
historical_cohort: Earlier cohorts used max_num_seqs=128 per replica; older released-runtime trials also had a 256-connection proxy cap or a smaller client window. All remain separate and are excluded from this cohort and its frontier.
telemetry: Five-second per-GPU and per-replica samples; ten-second client progress. Token rates use counter deltas. Backend request histograms include server queues and describe completing requests, not full pipeline latency. Both full-client and central60% descriptive windows were checked; central windows do not establish steady state. Proxy diagnostic counts are the last observed counters within each client interval.

runtime_source.status: Unmerged experimental build at measurement time; only four Slurm Python files differ from the baseline and all other dependency versions are pinned.

client_concurrency_semantics: Configured per-alias concurrency ceilings, shared across all five model columns. Queue-admission HTTP 429s can trigger client AIMD backoff and deferred retries; the ceiling is not a constant achieved concurrency.

extension_rule.reason: Neither topology improved valid throughput by10% at the final primary step; all four further candidates were skipped.
